explanation: The tail helps it balance on steep, rocky slopes in the mountains of Central Asia, and doubles as a blanket when it rests. Wide, furry paws work like snowshoes.

claims.text: Snow leopards wrap their long, thick tails around their faces and bodies for warmth.
Cheetahs, lynxes and jaguars do not use their tails as a wrap against the cold; lynxes have short tails.
A snow leopard's long tail helps it balance on steep, rocky terrain in the mountains of Central Asia.
Snow leopards have wide, furry paws that help them walk on snow.
